correctness.rationale: The degree-filtration argument proves both necessary conditions for ordinary potentials. The explicit cycle-power potential proves sufficiency when the cycle multiplicity is nonzero in the field. For hyperpotentials, endpoint-compatible path lengths force the cycle length to divide the truncation length plus one, and the explicit relations satisfy the required commutator identity and generate the truncation ideal.

evidence: Geiß et al., arXiv:2610.18805v1, Examples 6.2–6.3 and Theorem 6.6, gives the general framework and a single characteristic-two truncation example.

Chang and Tang, arXiv:2609.11200v1, Theorems 1.2–1.3, gives matrix Golod–Shafarevich–Vinberg obstructions and examples of quivers without Jacobi-finite potentials, but not the truncation classification.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Neither source implies the full criterion for every cycle length, Loewy length, and characteristic. The present result is a complete classification within the natural truncated-cycle family, not a claim about all finite-dimensional Jacobian algebras.

value.rationale: This is a complete classification of a natural family of truncated cyclic Nakayama presentations. It separates the combinatorial endpoint/length obstruction from the characteristic-dependent vanishing of the cyclic derivative coefficient, clarifying when hyperpotentials remain available although ordinary potentials fail.
